name: Small additive complements of the primes
description: construct() -> a nonempty subset B of [0,n=256] such that every integer in [256,512] is p+b for a prime p and b in B. Minimize |B|. All primes and target coverage are recomputed. Choose B in [0,256] so every integer in [256,512] is prime plus B, and minimize |B|. This only certifies finite coverage, not an asymptotic complement. The optimum is 10, established by an exact set-cover computation; this is a rediscovery task.

state_of_the_art.statement: The minimum is 10: {11, 16, 80, 117, 199, 204, 223, 225, 228, 242} covers [256,512]. Exact set-cover integer programmes show that 9 elements cannot. The programmes are split by parity, with every case of the prime 2 enumerated, and solved with HiGHS (scripts/check_state_of_the_art.py --slow). The asymptotic question is Erdős Problem #32.
